findings.summary: OCR dominates at 95.3% of wall time, while the busiest GPU averages 28.8% busy. The native backend caps region batches at 1; actual batching requires a backend experiment.
observations: The ordinary NACA call took 43.27 s: OCR 41.23 s, embedding 1.90 s, rendering 0.122 s and chunking 0.019 s. It follows one warm-up and is separate from the instrumented trace.

GPU 0/page 1 finished in 13.00 s, GPU 1/page 2 in 22.69 s and GPU 2/page 3 in 41.20 s. GPU 3 retained its replica without an assigned page. About 46.6% of the four-worker OCR time budget had assigned-page work; this is a scheduling measure, not compute utilization.

Average GPU busy during OCR was 11.0%, 16.4%, 28.8% and 0.0%. Average power was 35.8, 36.4, 43.4 and 27.8 W against 72 W limits. These samples show idle time, not percentages of peak arithmetic or memory bandwidth.

Each active worker captured 3 prefills and 29 decode forwards across its first recognition regions. Decode launched 901 GPU kernels per forward; matrix-vector kernels accounted for about 70.6% of sampled decode kernel time. CUDA correlation IDs attribute kernels to their launch phases.

All 71 NACA regions ended with EOS. The instrumented output passed the same exact OCR/chunk and cosine checks as the baseline. Known OCR errors in the frozen references remain documented in the baseline review.
Hardware counters for achieved SM throughput, DRAM bandwidth and occupancy were not collected. Trace occupancy annotations are theoretical; they are not measured occupancy.
findings.next_step: The requested batch-4 setting was overridden to 1 by the native backend; 465 recorded batches confirmed the limit. That trial is invalidated. Evaluate a supported serving backend at batch 1 before a separate batching comparison, keeping four GPUs and exact output checks.
findings.optimization: Test an inference backend that supports concurrent recognition regions, then vary region batch size after verifying fidelity to the native baseline.
